name: Pratt certificate monad for prime class hierarchy

phase_0.domain_name: Pratt certificate monad for prime class hierarchy
phase_0.boundary_condition: The terminal anchor of the Pratt certificate monad is the complete primality proof for a prime p, which requires verifying every prime factor of p−1 and recursively certifying each factor until reaching base primes 2 and 3. This constitutes the hermetic closure of the system: all branches of the certificate tree terminate in certified base cases, and the entire structure is self-contained within the finite descent of the prime class hierarchy.

VINIT.chosen_element: Uninitialized prime candidate before any Pratt certificate construction
VINIT.justification: Before a Pratt certificate can be assembled, the prime p exists only as a raw candidate with no witness chain, no factor decomposition, and no recursive sub-certificates. This is the void state: the candidate has not yet been subjected to the monadic structure that would embed it in the prime class hierarchy.

TANCH.chosen_element: The complete Pratt certificate tree for prime p
TANCH.justification: The terminal anchor is the fully constructed Pratt certificate, which is a finite rooted tree whose nodes are primes, whose edges are witness relationships, and whose leaves are base primes 2 and 3. This tree is the closed boundary that contains all recursive sub-certificates and constitutes a complete primality proof.

AFWD.chosen_element: Descent from p to its prime factors of p−1
AFWD.justification: The forward morphism in the Pratt certificate monad is the directed transformation from a prime p to the set of prime factors of p−1. Each factor must itself carry a Pratt certificate, so the morphism propagates downward through the prime class hierarchy, reducing the problem size at each step.

AREV.chosen_element: Ascent from certified factors back to the primality of p
AREV.justification: The contravariant morphism is the reverse transformation: once all prime factors of p−1 are certified, the ascent reconstructs the proof that p itself is prime. This descent-then-ascent is the solve/coagula cycle of the monad, where the downward split is reversed by the upward fuse.

CLINK.justification: CLINK chains together sequential morphisms in the certificate: the witness g for p, the factorization of p−1, and the recursive certificates for each factor. Each segment is composed with the next, forming the continuous witness chain that constitutes the full Pratt certificate.

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: The self-referential structure of the Pratt certificate monad
IMSCRIB.justification: IMSCRIB represents the identity: the certificate for p references certificates for its factors, which in turn reference certificates for their factors, and so on. The monad is self-similar — the structure of a certificate at any level mirrors the structure at every other level. The element is itself.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: Splitting prime p into its witness and the prime factors of p−1
FSPLIT.justification: FSPLIT branches the prime p into two arms: the T-arm carries the primitive root witness g that demonstrates the multiplicative order condition, and the F-arm carries the prime factorization of p−1, each factor requiring its own sub-certificate. The single prime p becomes the witness and the factor set.

FFUSE.chosen_element: Reconstituting primality of p from witness and certified factors
FFUSE.justification: FFUSE reunites the T-arm (witness g satisfying g^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p and g^((p−1)/q) ≠ 1 mod p for each factor q) and the F-arm (certified prime factors of p−1) to recover the complete proof that p is prime. FFUSE(FSPLIT(p)) = p, the original prime, now certified.

EVALT.chosen_element: Successful witness verification: g has correct multiplicative order modulo p
EVALT.justification: The affirmative branch evaluates to true when the primitive root witness g satisfies the order condition: g^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p and for every prime factor q of p−1, g^((p−1)/q) ≠ 1 mod p. This confirms g generates a subgroup of order p−1, proving p is prime.

EVALF.chosen_element: Failed witness verification: no valid primitive root found
EVALF.justification: The negative branch evaluates to false when the candidate witness g fails the order condition — either g^(p−1) ≠ 1 mod p, or g^((p−1)/q) ≡ 1 mod p for some factor q. This indicates the candidate is not a valid witness, and either p is composite or a different witness must be sought.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: Paradice state where witness is simultaneously valid and invalid
ENGAGR.justification: In the dialetheia state, the witness g both satisfies and fails the order condition — for example, when p is a pseudoprime to base g, where g^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p holds but p is actually composite. Both truth values are held without resolution: the surface condition is met while the deeper primality is not.

IFIX.chosen_element: Permanent recording of a certified prime in the proof tree
IFIX.justification: Once a prime p has been fully certified — witness verified and all factors of p−1 recursively certified — the result is irreversibly fixed as a leaf or internal node in the Pratt certificate tree. This record cannot be undone; it becomes part of the permanent structure of the proof.

phase_2.split_element: FSPLIT on prime p: branches into witness g (T-arm) and prime factorization of p−1 (F-arm)
split_outputs: Primitive root witness g satisfying order conditions
Set of prime factors of p−1 each requiring recursive certification
phase_2.fuse_element: FFUSE: reunites witness g and certified factors of p−1 to recover primality of p
phase_2.fuse_result: Prime p, now certified as prime via complete Pratt certificate

phase_3.void_description: State 00: Prime candidate p exists as a raw integer with no witness, no factorization of p−1, and no recursive sub-certificates. The monadic structure has not yet been applied.
phase_3.true_description: State 01: Witness g satisfies the multiplicative order condition modulo p, and all prime factors of p−1 are certified. The Pratt certificate for p is complete and valid.
phase_3.false_description: State 10: Either no valid primitive root witness exists for p, or at least one prime factor of p−1 fails its recursive certification. The candidate p cannot be certified as prime.
phase_3.both_description: State 11: A paradice where the witness condition is simultaneously satisfied and violated — for instance, p is a pseudoprime to base g, where g^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p holds but p is composite. Both truth values coexist without resolution.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the Pratt certificate monad with an unverified prime candidate p in void state 00, carrying no witness chain or factor decomposition.
Split prime p into two branches — T-arm receives the primitive root witness g, F-arm receives the prime factorization of p−1.
Evaluate the T-arm by checking that g^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p and g^((p−1)/q) ≠ 1 mod p for each prime factor q of p−1, confirming g is a valid witness.
Descend from each prime factor q of p−1 into its own Pratt certificate construction, applying the forward morphism to reduce the problem to smaller primes.
Initialize sub-candidate for each prime factor q of p−1 in void state, beginning recursive certification.
Split each factor q into its witness and the factorization of q−1, creating nested sub-branches.
Verify the witness for each factor q satisfies the order condition, confirming q is prime.
Continue descending through the prime class hierarchy, reducing each factor until reaching base primes 2 and 3.
Verify base prime 2 has trivial witness (no factors of 2−1=1 to check), confirming it is prime.
Verify base prime 3 has trivial witness (no factors of 3−1=2 beyond the already-certified base prime 2), confirming it is prime.
Ascend from the certified base primes 2 and 3 back up through the factor tree, reconstructing primality at each level.
Compose the witness chain segments — link the verified witness g for p with the certified factors of p−1 into a continuous proof structure.
Apply self-reference: the structure of the certificate for p mirrors the structure for each factor q, maintaining the monadic identity across all levels.
Fuse the T-arm (verified witness g) and F-arm (certified prime factors of p−1) to reconstitute the complete primality proof for p, satisfying FFUSE(FSPLIT(p)) = p.
Permanently fix the certified prime p into the Pratt certificate tree as an append-only record, closing this branch of the proof.
The terminal anchor closes the system — the complete Pratt certificate tree for p is a finite, self-contained primality proof with all branches terminating in base primes 2 and 3.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The Pratt certificate compiler translates a prime candidate p into the sequence of operations: factor p−1, find a witness g, recursively certify each factor, and assemble the proof tree. It is the monadic bind that threads the certificate construction through each level of the prime class hierarchy.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Components communicate through the witness chain: the factorization module passes prime factors to the recursive certification module, which returns certified sub-certificates. The witness verification module receives the candidate witness and factor set, returning a boolean evaluation. All communication flows along the directed edges of the certificate tree.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: State is stored as the Pratt certificate tree itself — each node is a prime with its witness and child certificates. The tree is immutable once constructed, serving as both the computation trace and the permanent proof record. Intermediate states are ephemeral; only the final fixed tree persists.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The scheduler determines the order of recursive certification: it processes factors of p−1 in ascending order, ensuring that smaller primes are certified before larger ones that depend on them. The schedule is depth-first, following each branch to its base case before returning to fuse the results.
phase_5.alfs_store: The canonical reference store is the set of base primes {2, 3} which are axiomatically certified without further recursion. These are the bootstrap seeds from which all higher Pratt certificates are constructed. The store also includes known primitive roots for small primes, serving as cached witnesses to avoid recomputation.

phase_6.cycle_cost: Each operation cycle consumes computational work: factoring p−1, testing witness conditions modulo p, and recursively certifying factors. The cost is measured in modular exponentiations and integer factorizations, which are the fundamental operations of the certificate monad.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Before the cycle: prime candidate p is unverified, p−1 is unfactored, no witness has been tested, and no sub-certificates exist. The system is in a state of maximum uncertainty about p's primality.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: After the cycle: p is either certified prime (complete Pratt certificate tree constructed and fixed) or certified composite (witness verification failed). The certificate tree is permanently recorded, and the system state has been resolved to a definitive truth value.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The Pratt certificate monad is entropy-conservative because the computational work invested in factoring p−1 and verifying witnesses is exactly balanced by the information gained: the complete primality proof. No information is lost or created; the certificate is a lossless encoding of the primality decision. The recursive structure ensures that work at each level is proportional to the information extracted at that level, maintaining a zero net entropy change across the entire proof tree.
